I love township so much but the developers have changed directions so I thought I would give this one a go. They don't have a spooky amusement park to start -_-

I don't love it. I hate it. If you want to find yourself sitting in a water barrel sobbing "I don't belong here, I feel it... my life is like death" play this one.

I did not skip the intro, [b]please do[/b], severance job vibes and you cannot skip once it starts. 

I passed out in my own yard unaware I needed to sleep. Woke up to find a $50 bill as a medical team had to carry me to bed. What's next property taxes? Don't boss me around in my own yard pls. If I want to stay up and garden at 3am that's what I'm going to do. Imagine playing Requiem and having to put Leon down for a nap or he dies xD

Unless I can be Kissing Kate Barlow or in the least Sheriff and put the whole medical team in jail I don't want to play again. Maybe if I got to design the medical team character as someone and see him carry me to bed I'd have a little more patience with this night-night nonsense. 

And to make matters worse you don't even get cute pajamas, slippers, or a mask. No bathroom or shower. If you're going to force bedtime there needs to be more whimsy around it. Have a little spider come out say goodnight and blow a kiss. People could pick what they want: a ghost, firefly, mouse, spider, a friendly shadow etc. to tell them goodnight. Imagine a firefly buzzing goodnight in glowing letters. Change things up sometimes you hear animals etc. outside. 

I tried playing one more time after writing this review as I saw a beautiful fall screenshot but even with the terrible map, heading back before sundown was too much panic not enough cozy for me. I want to explore and design freely and the bed optional like in fortnite lego. This game is not an escape from reality but rather just another dimension of it. One where you stay in your own filth.

At first this game did not hook me at all but as someone who likes to 100% games, I was determined to play it through fully. 

It's a well made game I'll give it to the dev. You can really tell that there's one brain behind it all. I love the details and the hidden secrets, the notes that you have to carefully read and solve mysteries, all the characters and their unique personalities, schedule, character development. While it seems like a chill game, you really need to pay a lot of attention and plan ahead. 

It's a grindy game and it takes quite some days to get the first achievement which in my opinion is pretty nice to not instantly get that dopamine kick. Rather it will reward you after you've worked hard enough. Most things are so expensive in this game, but I guess that's part of the grind. It's not easy and you have to figure out the best way to play this game, what to focus on, what sell price is the best, plan ahead based on day and season, and so on. Slowly you get rewarded in different ways. 

Early game is intensive, slow, and confusing. Mid game you start to get a hang of everything, and start the real money making and crafting grind, motivation to play can be on and off here. End game is kinda odd and confusing. That's when you finally get max level of everything and that's when you get the real "support" that I would have appreciate if I had them earlier. To me it makes no sense, especially the [spoiler]obelisks[/spoiler]. What is the point of having access to the "support" crafts/items after completing everything in the late game stage?

Overall, a fun game. It fits many play-styles like those who want to just farm and craft, those who like to fish, those who like to slay monsters. I wish you could save anytime during the day like the smartphone version, don't understand why that's not a thing on PC. But good game!

What I really love about it is that it’s incredibly relaxing and cozy, but at the same time it has much more depth than you might expect at first. You can just chill, build up your farm, go fishing, take care of animals, make friends, and explore the world. But if you want more, there are also plenty of challenges.

That balance is what makes Stardew Valley so great. Some things can be difficult in the beginning, but through grinding, better equipment, planning, and preparation, you can make things much easier for yourself. Progress always feels rewarding without the game ever feeling unfair.

You can play Stardew Valley in a completely relaxed way, but if you want to, you can also min-max everything, plan the perfect daily routine, optimize your profits, and get the most out of your farm. The game gives you total freedom to play however you like.

For me, Stardew Valley is an absolute masterpiece: charming, motivating, relaxing, and deep enough to keep you entertained for hundreds of hours.

I loved Harvest Moon growing up, and this managed to do something rare with something you're nostalgic over: Stardew Valley is better than Harvest Moon. The artstyle, the soundtrack, the gameplay loop, the modding community, the coziest of cozy atmospheres. This game is like a warm hug from a loved one. This game is the benchmark that all other farming sims are measured by, and that standard is met only by its creator Concerned Ape. Creating the game almost single-handedly, he continued to work on it for over a decade and gave us so much content that he could easily have packaged as DLC and we all would have paid it...but I suppose as we left Joja Corp. behind so did he. He rejected the capitalist demand for profit and gave us major update after major update for FREE. I think I paid $10 for this game and it is *easily* one of my Top 3 games of all time. No other game will give you the same value for its cost as Stardew Valley. 

10/10 Perfect Game

Stardew Valley is one of those games that feels like a second home. It starts as a simple farming game, but the more time you spend in Pelican Town, the more you realize there’s so much more to do than just grow crops.

The freedom is what makes it special. You can spend your days farming, fishing, mining, exploring, decorating your farm, raising animals, or just getting to know the villagers. There’s no pressure to play a certain way, and somehow even small things like organizing your farm or catching a rare fish feel rewarding.

The characters are probably one of the best parts. Every villager has their own personality and story, and getting to know them makes the town feel alive. The little events, seasonal changes, and small details make it feel like an actual place instead of just a game map.

The amount of content is honestly crazy for a game made mostly by one person. There’s always something to work toward, whether it’s improving your farm, completing collections, unlocking areas, or just making your perfect little life.

The only downside is that the beginning can feel a bit slow, and if farming or relaxing games aren’t your thing, it might not hook you immediately. Some systems also take time to understand.

But once it clicks, it’s hard to put down. It’s relaxing when you want it to be, but it can also become surprisingly addictive when you start optimizing everything.

Stardew Valley is a farming simulation RPG developed by ConcernedApe that proves relaxing games can be just as engaging as action-packed adventures. What begins as a simple journey to restore an abandoned farm becomes a deeply rewarding experience filled with exploration, relationships, farming, crafting, and personal growth. Stardew Valley creates a peaceful world where players can progress at their own pace while constantly discovering new activities and goals.

The game's greatest strength is its freedom. Players are never forced into one specific playstyle. Some may focus on creating the most successful farm possible, while others may spend their time fishing, mining, building relationships with villagers, or exploring the mysterious areas surrounding the town. The game allows players to decide what success means to them, creating an experience that feels personal.

Farming is the foundation of Stardew Valley, and the progression system makes every improvement feel meaningful. Starting with a small collection of tools and a messy piece of land, players slowly transform their farm into a thriving operation. Planting crops, raising animals, upgrading equipment, and expanding the farm creates a satisfying feeling of growth that encourages players to keep improving.

The characters and relationships are another major part of what makes Stardew Valley special. The villagers each have their own personalities, stories, and daily routines, making the town feel alive. Building friendships and learning more about the characters creates a stronger connection to the world and gives players another reason to return every day.

Beyond farming, Stardew Valley offers a surprising amount of additional content. Mining provides adventure and combat, fishing offers a relaxing challenge, and seasonal events give the world a sense of time and progression. The game constantly introduces new goals without overwhelming the player, creating a perfect balance between relaxation and motivation.

The only major downside of Stardew Valley is that its slow pace may not appeal to everyone. Players looking for constant action or fast progression may find the experience too calm. Some systems can also take time to understand, especially for new players who are unfamiliar with farming games.

However, these qualities are also what make Stardew Valley so enjoyable. It is a game about patience, creativity, and creating a life in a world that feels welcoming. With charming characters, endless customization, relaxing gameplay, and incredible attention to detail, Stardew Valley remains one of the best examples of how simple ideas can create unforgettable experiences.
